S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers shall report any battery thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, property damage, or emergency-service response to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware, with a detailed incident report within 10 business days. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers promptly when an incident presents a material safety risk, and provide updated safety information as it becomes available.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall report any battery thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, property damage, or emergency-service response to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware, with a detailed incident report within 10 business days. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers promptly when an incident presents a material safety risk, and provide updated safety information as it becomes available. Reports shall include known incidents regardless of whether the cause is confirmed; manufacturers shall promptly investigate and correct previously omitted reports.

parameters.quote: Each model shall undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol before market authorization and after material design changes. Manufacturers shall submit per-model results, including units tested and failure rate, confidentially to the regulator and provide the exact results to customers of that model. A model exceeding a 5% failure rate shall complete corrective action and retesting under regulator oversight. A model exceeding 7.5% shall not be authorized for sale, or shall be suspended from sale, until corrective action is completed and it passes a retest at or below 7.5%.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: Each model shall undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol before market authorization and after material design changes. Manufacturers shall submit per-model results, including units tested and failure rate, confidentially to the regulator and provide the exact results to customers of that model. A model exceeding a 5% failure rate shall complete corrective action and retesting under regulator oversight. A model exceeding 7.5% shall not be authorized for sale, or shall be suspended from sale, until corrective action is completed and it passes a retest at or below 7.5%.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model shall undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol before market authorization and after material design changes. Manufacturers shall submit per-model results, including units tested and failure rate, confidentially to the regulator and provide the exact results to customers of that model. A model exceeding a 5% failure rate shall complete corrective action and retesting under regulator oversight. A model exceeding 7.5% shall not be authorized for sale, or shall be suspended from sale, until corrective action is completed and it passes a retest at or below 7.5%. Regulators may require additional measures where evidence indicates an unacceptable risk.

parameters.quote: New battery units placed on the market shall support remote emergency shut-off no later than three years after this standard takes effect. For units already installed when the standard takes effect, manufacturers shall provide a compatible retrofit or replacement option and complete required retrofits within six years, where technically feasible.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: New battery units placed on the market shall support remote emergency shut-off no later than three years after this standard takes effect. For units already installed when the standard takes effect, manufacturers shall provide a compatible retrofit or replacement option and complete required retrofits within six years, where technically feasible.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: New battery units placed on the market shall support remote emergency shut-off no later than three years after this standard takes effect. Manufacturers shall provide clear instructions for using the function and ensure it can be activated by authorized emergency responders. For units already installed when the standard takes effect, manufacturers shall provide a compatible retrofit or replacement option and complete required retrofits within six years, where technically feasible. If a retrofit is not technically feasible, the manufacturer shall notify affected customers and the regulator and provide an alternative safety measure.

parameters.quote: New battery units shall include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after this standard takes effect.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: New battery units shall include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after this standard takes effect.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New battery units shall include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after this standard takes effect. Manufacturers shall provide customers and regulators with information on the suppression system and its maintenance.

parameters.quote: If any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer shall notify the regulator and affected customers promptly and initiate a recall, including a repair, replacement, or refund plan. Regulators may require a recall at a lower incident rate where the evidence indicates an unacceptable risk.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: If any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer shall notify the regulator and affected customers promptly and initiate a recall, including a repair, replacement, or refund plan. Regulators may require a recall at a lower incident rate where the evidence indicates an unacceptable risk.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall provide customers clear safety notices about material risks, incidents, and required actions, and promptly update notices as new information becomes available. If any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer shall notify the regulator and affected customers promptly and initiate a recall, including a repair, replacement, or refund plan. Regulators may require a recall at a lower incident rate where the evidence indicates an unacceptable risk.

judge_section_notes: The final rules are strict on incident reporting (24h all incidents) and S5 recall trigger at 8/100k with no transition, which hits Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9) but spares Northwind's Hearth 10 (6.4). S2 sets a 55°C test with a 5% corrective-action threshold and a 7.5% sales cap, keeping per-model results confidential to regulators but giving exact results to customers. S3 gives a 6-year retrofit deadline (Northwind red line) but a 3-year new-unit deadline, while S4 requires built-in suppression at 36 months (Halcyon red line).
